findings.recommendation: Add a Textarea component mirroring Input.jsx exactly (same border-input, bg-background/60, shadow-sm, focus-visible ring/border, min-h-[96px]) and use it here. This guarantees the contact form matches every other field and stays in sync if tokens change.

findings.title: maxResults field copy and the help text carry the explanatory load instead of a clean label + caption
findings.current: Label text is the full sentence 'How many recent emails to scan per sync (1–50)' sitting directly above a 112px-wide number input plus a Save button on the same row.
findings.problem: Long labels-as-instructions are an anti-pattern in Apple settings; the control range and explanation should be a short caption, and a bare number input with no stepper/units feels unfinished next to a switch-rich UI.
findings.recommendation: Label → 'Emails scanned per sync'; add a caption below in text-xs muted: 'Between 1 and 50 most recent messages.' Consider a small Slider or +/- stepper for a more tactile feel, or at minimum suffix the input visually with 'emails'. Keep input ~96-112px and align Save trailing.

findings.title: Page transition is a 150ms easeOut fade — flat, no depth, no stagger
findings.current: Entering pages animate opacity 0→1 and y 6→0 over duration 0.15 ease 'easeOut'; this wraps the whole Settings grid as one block.
findings.problem: A uniform 150ms easeOut is serviceable but generic; Settings, being a list of distinct groups, is a natural place for a gentle staggered reveal that signals craft. Nothing here uses spring physics despite Framer Motion being in the stack.
findings.recommendation: On Settings, wrap the cards in a motion stagger (container staggerChildren 0.05, child initial y:8 opacity:0 → spring stiffness 260 damping 26). Keep the global PageTransition but let groups settle in sequence (≤250ms total) so the screen assembles with calm confidence rather than a single fade.

findings.title: Switch hit target is below comfortable size and has no offset-aware focus ring on dark bg
findings.current: Root is 20px tall; focus-visible uses ring-2 ring-ring with ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background. Disabled state is opacity-50.
findings.problem: 20px tall is a small target (Apple recommends ~44px tappable area); the disabled opacity-50 during async toggles makes the control look broken rather than busy, and there's no busy/pending micro-state distinct from disabled.
findings.recommendation: Beyond enlarging (see motion finding), add an 'is-saving' state: keep the switch full-opacity but show a 12px Loader2 spinner overlapping the thumb or a subtle pulse, instead of dimming to 50%. Ensure the tap area is ≥44px via padding on the row label so users can hit it easily on mobile (BottomNav exists, so mobile matters).

premiumOpportunities: Make AI/alerts toggles iconic: a true iOS-grade switch (28x46px, spring thumb that elongates on press, 200ms color sweep) is the single highest-leverage 'wow' on this page since the toggles are the hero interaction. Pair the AI toggle with a tiny live status chip ('Local model ready' / 'Ollama offline') so flipping it feels consequential and trustworthy.

Convert the disconnect into a signature destructive flow: an AlertDialog with backdrop-blur, spring-in panel, and a confirm button that requires a deliberate press — plus an optional 'type your email to confirm' for true gravity given it nukes all app data. Apple-grade friction on the one dangerous action sells the whole app's seriousness.

Animated connected-account card: a soft, slow-breathing risk-safe glow ring (#34c77b at low alpha, 4-6s ease-in-out loop) around the avatar to communicate a healthy, live connection at a glance — calm reassurance instead of an inert key/value box.

Settings-as-grouped-list redesign: single max-w-2xl column with inset-grouped sections (rounded-2xl, hairline dividers, tinted 32px icon chips) so it reads exactly like iOS Settings — instantly familiar, deferential, content-first.

Inline auto-save with micro-confirmation: drop most explicit Save buttons (iOS-style), persist on blur/change, and confirm with a brief inline check that springs in next to the field (opacity+scale, settle 220ms) rather than a corner toast — making the page feel effortless and 'just works'.
Staggered assembly on entry: groups settle in with a 50ms stagger and gentle spring, giving the screen a crafted, composed feel the moment it loads.

findings.currentStateSummary: Motion in SecureInbox is ad-hoc and thin. Framer Motion is used in exactly 6 places (PageTransition, StatCard, VerdictBanner, AppShell AnimatePresence, EmailDetailPage collapse, LoginPage password-rules collapse), every one with a hand-typed tween: durations of 0.15s / 0.2s / 0.3s and string easings ('easeOut', 'easeInOut') with no shared config. There are zero springs, zero whileHover/whileTap press feedback, zero layout/layoutId animations, and no useReducedMotion/MotionConfig anywhere. CSS interactivity is limited to Tailwind transition-colors / transition-all using the framework default 150ms ease, so hovers are flat color swaps with no scale or depth. Lists (inbox rows, dashboard risky list) have no enter or stagger animation, verdict changes after a review snap with no transition, and a bespoke useCountUp RAF loop reimplements number animation that Framer already provides. The result reads as "functional React" rather than the calm, spring-driven, tactile feel of an Apple-grade product.

findings.title: No shared motion vocabulary — every animation invents its own duration & easing
findings.current: Five independent transition objects: PageTransition `{duration:0.15, ease:'easeOut'}`, StatCard `{duration:0.3, ease:'easeOut', delay}`, VerdictBanner `{duration:0.2, ease:'easeOut'}`, EmailDetailPage collapse `{duration:0.2, ease:'easeInOut'}`, LoginPage collapse `{duration:0.2, ease:'easeInOut'}`. No constants file, no tokens.
findings.problem: Apple motion feels like one system because timing and curves are shared. Here, three different durations and two different easings appear across five surfaces with no rationale — page transitions are faster (150ms) than a stat card fade (300ms), so navigating then watching cards settle feels disjointed. 'easeOut'/'easeInOut' are generic CSS curves, not the gentle decelerate of a spring; nothing feels physical.
findings.recommendation: Create `frontend/src/lib/motion.js` exporting a shared vocabulary and import it everywhere. Springs for entrances/layout, a single tween for micro color/opacity. Concretely: `export const springSoft = { type:'spring', stiffness:380, damping:32, mass:0.9 }` (UI default), `springSnappy = { type:'spring', stiffness:520, damping:30 }` (press/toggles), `const ease = [0.32, 0.72, 0, 1]` (Apple-style decelerate), `const dur = { fast:0.18, base:0.26, slow:0.4 }`. Replace all five inline objects with these. Standardize entrance distance to `y:8` (not the current mix of 6/10/-4).

findings.title: Nothing uses spring physics — all motion is tween-based
findings.current: Every Framer animation is a duration+ease tween. grep for `type:'spring'`, `stiffness`, `damping`, `useSpring` returns zero hits across src/.
findings.problem: The defining quality of Apple/iOS motion is spring physics: elements arrive with momentum and settle naturally, never on a fixed clock. Linear-duration tweens feel mechanical and 'web-default'. For a premium security tool, the entrance of a verdict banner or stat card should feel like it has weight, not like a CSS keyframe.
findings.recommendation: Switch entrance/layout animations to springs from the new motion lib (`transition={springSoft}`). Drop explicit `duration` for spring transitions (it conflicts). For StatCard and VerdictBanner use `springSoft`; for press/toggle feedback use `springSnappy`. Keep tweens only for pure opacity/color cross-fades where a spring would overshoot oddly.

findings.title: No press / tap feedback anywhere — buttons, rows, filter chips feel non-tactile
findings.current: Button uses `transition-all` + `hover:bg-primary/90` only — no `active:` scale. EmailRow has `transition-colors hover:bg-accent/50` and no press state. Filter chips: `transition-colors` color swap only. grep for `whileTap`/`active:scale` returns nothing.
findings.problem: On Apple surfaces every actionable element confirms the touch with a subtle scale-down (the 'press'). Without it, clicking Re-scan, Safe/Phishing, or a filter chip feels dead — there's no tactile confirmation, which undermines the 'just works' confidence a security action needs.
findings.recommendation: Add a press transform to all primary interactive elements. For the shadcn Button add `active:scale-[0.97] transition-transform` to the base cva string (keep `transition-all` for color). For EmailRow and filter chips add `active:scale-[0.99]`. Better: a reusable `<MotionButton>` wrapping Button with `whileTap={{ scale: 0.97 }} whileHover={{ scale: 1.01 }} transition={springSnappy}`. Use scale 0.97 for buttons, 0.99 for large rows so the effect is proportional.

findings.title: Inbox & dashboard lists have no enter/stagger animation
findings.current: Email rows render as plain `<Link>` inside `.map()` with no Framer wrapper and no stagger. The dashboard 'risky' list and inbox groups appear instantly. Only the 4 StatCards stagger (via `staggerIndex` prop → manual `delay`).
findings.problem: When inbox content loads or a filter changes, rows pop in all at once with zero motion — the single least-polished moment in the app, and it's the primary surface. Apple lists gently cascade in on first paint. The existing StatCard stagger is also implemented by hand (prop-drilled index → delay) instead of Framer's parent/child orchestration, so it's inconsistent with how lists should work.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each inbox group's row container and the dashboard list in a Framer parent with `variants={{ show:{ transition:{ staggerChildren:0.035, delayChildren:0.04 } } }}` and give EmailRow an `item` variant `{ hidden:{opacity:0, y:8}, show:{opacity:1, y:0, transition:springSoft} }`. Cap stagger so a full page (25 rows) finishes under ~450ms — use `staggerChildren:0.03` and consider `AnimatePresence` with `mode='popLayout'` so removed rows (after mark-phishing) animate out. Refactor StatCard to use the same parent-variant stagger and delete the `staggerIndex` prop + manual `delayS`.

findings.title: Verdict change after a manual review snaps with no transition
findings.current: VerdictBanner only animates on initial mount (`initial/animate`). When ReviewActions marks an email safe/phishing and `onReviewed` updates the bucket, the banner's color, icon, and label change instantly because the new state isn't keyed for AnimatePresence and there's no transition on `tone.soft`/`tone.text` color classes.
findings.problem: The verdict banner is THE payoff moment of this app — a user reviews an email and the security verdict updates. Right now that critical state change is a hard cut with no acknowledgement, which feels cheap and can be missed entirely. Color classes also change without `transition-colors`, so even the background snaps.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the banner in `<AnimatePresence mode='wait'>` and give `motion.div` a `key={riskBucket}` so a verdict change cross-fades + slides (`initial={{opacity:0, y:-6}} animate={{opacity:1, y:0}} exit={{opacity:0, y:6}} transition={springSoft}`). Add `transition-colors duration-300` to the banner so soft-bg/text shifts are smooth. Pair with a Sonner success toast on review so the user gets dual confirmation.

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion support
findings.current: No `useReducedMotion`, no `<MotionConfig reducedMotion>`, and index.css has no `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block. The count-up RAF loop in StatCard:7 also ignores the OS setting.
findings.problem: An accessibility and premium baseline: Apple respects Reduce Motion system-wide. Animated count-ups, page slides, and staggered lists can cause discomfort for vestibular-sensitive users, and shipping a thesis-grade app without honoring the OS preference is a clear gap.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the app in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion='user'>` in main.jsx so all Framer animations auto-degrade to instant/opacity-only. In useCountUp, early-return the final value when `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`. Add a global CSS guard: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ *,*::before,*::after{ animation-duration:.01ms!important; transition-duration:.01ms!important } }`.

findings.title: Collapsible height animations use easeInOut tween — choppy and slow to feel premium
findings.current: Both 'Scan details' and the password-rules list animate `height: 0 → 'auto'` with `{duration:0.2, ease:'easeInOut'}`. The chevron rotates with CSS `transition-transform duration-200` (EmailDetailPage:246) — a third, separately-tuned timing.
findings.problem: Animating to `height:'auto'` with a symmetric easeInOut tween reads as generic accordion behavior; the content inside doesn't fade with the right offset and the chevron's 200ms CSS curve doesn't match the 200ms-but-different-feel Framer curve, so the disclosure and its caret drift apart. Apple disclosures spring open with content that settles.
findings.recommendation: Use `springSoft` for the height animation and animate the chevron with the SAME Framer spring (`<motion.span animate={{ rotate: scanExpanded ? 0 : -90 }} transition={springSoft}>`) so caret and panel move as one. Add a small content offset (`initial={{opacity:0, y:-4}}`) so revealed content eases down rather than appearing flat. Keep `overflow-hidden`.

findings.title: Hand-rolled useCountUp duplicates Framer and is decoupled from the card entrance
findings.current: A 30-line RAF `useCountUp` with cubic ease-out runs for 600ms after a `staggerIndex*60ms` delay, while the card's opacity/y entrance is a separate 300ms tween at `delayS`. Two timing systems for one component.
findings.problem: Reinventing number animation adds maintenance surface and risks desync: the number starts counting at 600ms duration while the card finishes appearing at 300ms, so the count keeps ticking after the card has fully settled, which looks slightly unfinished. It also ignores reduced-motion.
findings.recommendation: Replace useCountUp with Framer's `useMotionValue` + `animate(mv, target, { duration:1, ease:[0.32,0.72,0,1] })` and render via `useTransform(mv, v => Math.round(v))`, or keep the RAF but align its duration/curve to the shared `ease` token and gate it on reduced-motion. Tie the count start to the card's entrance completion (via `onAnimationComplete`) so number and card feel like one event.

findings.title: Page transition is too subtle and AnimatePresence mode='wait' adds a perceptible gap
findings.current: PageTransition: `initial {opacity:0,y:6}` → `animate {y:0}` → `exit {opacity:0,y:-4}`, 150ms easeOut, inside `<AnimatePresence mode='wait' initial={false}>`.
findings.problem: `mode='wait'` fully unmounts the old page before mounting the new one, so with a 150ms out + 150ms in there's a ~300ms blank-ish beat on every navigation between Inbox/Dashboard/Settings — the chrome (sidebar) stays but content flashes empty. The 6px travel is so small it's barely a transition; it neither commits to a clean cross-fade nor to a directional slide.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) keep `mode='wait'` but make it a fast confident cross-fade with slight scale: `initial={{opacity:0, y:10, scale:0.99}} animate={{opacity:1, y:0, scale:1}} transition={springSoft}` and a quick `exit={{opacity:0, transition:{duration:0.12}}}`, or (b) drop `mode='wait'` for an overlapping cross-fade so there's no empty gap. Recommend (a). Increase travel to y:10 so the motion is legible.

findings.title: Hovers are flat color-only — no depth, lift, or scale on cards and rows
findings.current: Card is a static `shadow-sm` with no hover state. EmailRow hover is `hover:bg-accent/50` (background tint only). StatCards don't react to hover at all.
findings.problem: Apple 'depth' principle: interactive surfaces subtly lift toward the user on hover (shadow + faint scale/border-glow). Flat background swaps make the UI feel like a static document rather than a responsive surface, and the StatCards being completely inert on hover misses an easy premium cue.
findings.recommendation: For clickable cards/rows add `transition-[transform,box-shadow,border-color] duration-200 hover:-translate-y-px hover:shadow-md hover:border-border/80`. For EmailRow, on hover also brighten the left risk border. For StatCards add a faint `hover:bg-elevated` lift. Keep effects subtle (1px translate, shadow-md max) to stay calm and security-appropriate — avoid large lifts.

findings.title: ScoreBar fill animates via transition-all with no entrance, score bars snap on mount
findings.current: The score bar fill is a `<div className='... transition-all' style={{ width: pct% }}>`. On first render the width is set directly, so `transition-all` only fires on subsequent changes — the bar appears already full with no fill-in animation.
findings.problem: Risk-score bars are a key trust/explainability signal (rule signals vs AI signals). Having them pop in fully-filled wastes a natural, satisfying reveal that would draw the eye to the breakdown. `transition-all` also animates every property (color, padding) which is wasteful and can cause jank.
findings.recommendation: Animate the fill from 0 on mount with Framer: `<motion.div initial={{width:0}} animate={{width: pct + '%'}} transition={{ ...springSoft, delay: 0.05 }} />`, ideally staggered (Total → Rule → AI). Replace `transition-all` with `transition-[width]` (or `transition-colors` separately) to avoid animating unrelated properties.

findings.title: MobileSync FAB only animates opacity while syncing — no enter/exit
findings.current: The floating sync button is a plain `<button>` that returns `null` when not connected, with `transition-opacity` and an `animate-spin` icon while syncing.
findings.problem: A floating action button that appears/disappears with no scale/fade-in feels abrupt on mobile (the most touch-tactile context). It also has no press feedback, so the primary mobile action gives no tactile response.
findings.recommendation: Wrap in `<AnimatePresence>` and animate `initial={{opacity:0, scale:0.8}} animate={{opacity:1, scale:1}} exit={{opacity:0, scale:0.8}} transition={springSnappy}`. Add `whileTap={{ scale: 0.9 }}`. This is a quick, high-visibility polish win.

findings.title: Skeletons use a generic pulse instead of a directional shimmer
findings.current: Skeleton is `animate-pulse` (opacity throb) on `bg-muted/70`. DashboardPage also inlines two `animate-pulse` bars.
findings.problem: Opacity pulse is the most generic loading affordance; premium apps use a left-to-right shimmer gradient that signals 'content is streaming in' and matches the directional feel of the rest of the motion system. Inlined pulse bars also bypass the Skeleton component, risking drift.
findings.recommendation: Define a shimmer keyframe in index.css (`@keyframes shimmer { 100% { transform: translateX(100%) } }`) and a `--color` gradient overlay, or swap to a `bg-gradient-to-r` with `animate-[shimmer_1.5s_infinite]` masked element. Apply inside Skeleton and replace the two inline DashboardPage bars with `<Skeleton>`.

findings.title: Chevron/disclosure timings are tuned independently from their panels
findings.current: index.css defines radius and color tokens but NO motion tokens (no `--duration-*`, no `--ease-*`). CSS transitions therefore rely on per-element Tailwind classes (`duration-200`, default 150ms) tuned separately from Framer values.
findings.problem: Two parallel timing systems (CSS Tailwind durations vs Framer JS transitions) with no shared source of truth guarantees long-term drift — e.g. the chevron's CSS 200ms vs its panel's Framer 200ms-but-different-curve. Apple-grade systems centralize timing.
findings.recommendation: Add motion tokens to the `@theme` block in index.css: `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); --duration-fast:180ms; --duration-base:260ms;` and use them in CSS (`transition-timing-function: var(--ease-out)`). Mirror the exact same numbers in `lib/motion.js` so JS and CSS animations share one feel. Prefer driving disclosure carets from Framer (see ScanDetails finding) to eliminate the dual system entirely.

premiumOpportunities: Signature 'verdict reveal' moment: when a scan completes or a manual review lands, animate the VerdictBanner with a single confident spring (cross-fade keyed on riskBucket) plus a one-shot, color-matched glow pulse on its border (safe=green, quarantine=rose) that fades in ~600ms and never repeats. This turns the core security payoff into a memorable, calm, trustworthy beat — the app's emotional centerpiece — without resorting to alarm-red flashing.

Shared-element transition from inbox row to email detail: give EmailRow's risk left-border and sender a `layoutId` (e.g. `verdict-${id}`) so navigating into EmailDetailPage morphs the row's risk accent into the VerdictBanner via Framer `layout`. This is the most iOS-like interaction available here and makes the inbox→detail flow feel continuous instead of a hard route swap.

Animated, staggered score-bar reveal in ScanDetails: on expand, fill Total → Rule signals → AI signals bars in sequence with springs and count-up numbers, so the explainability breakdown 'draws itself' — directly reinforcing the thesis's XAI angle (showing WHY a verdict was reached) through motion.

Orchestrated inbox cascade on load and on filter change: a subtle staggered row entrance (30ms apart) using AnimatePresence popLayout, so filtering by risk bucket re-flows the list smoothly and marking an email as phishing animates it out and lets the rest settle — making list mutations feel physical and intentional.

Global spring-physics foundation via a single lib/motion.js + <MotionConfig>: adopting one spring config (stiffness 380 / damping 32) across page transitions, cards, banners, toggles and presses would instantly unify the whole app's feel — the highest-leverage change to move from 'functional React' to 'Apple-grade cohesion'.

findings.currentStateSummary: Three transactional templates live in backend/extras/notifications/email.template.js: a welcome email (purple 135deg gradient + emoji confetti), a monthly digest (dark-navy header + plain white metric table), and a phishing alert (red 135deg gradient + siren emoji). All use a layout div with max-width 600-680px centered on a light grey body, inline styles, and 'Segoe UI', Arial fallback. Each looks like it came from a different product: three different header treatments, three different accent palettes, and none of them match the app's real brand (bg #0a0d14, primary #3b9eff, Inter) or the canonical 6-bucket risk hexes in risk.js. They are functional and reasonably escaped, but visually generic-SaaS, not Apple-grade, and they have real client-compatibility liabilities: outer layout is a div (not a table), there is no role=presentation table scaffold, no MSO/Outlook conditional wrapper, no dark-mode meta or color-scheme handling, no preheader, no logo, and critically no CTA button at all even though the alert copy literally tells the user to "open SecureInbox."

findings.title: No CTA button anywhere — the alert tells users to act but gives them nothing to click
findings.current: The phishing alert body says 'Please open SecureInbox and review these emails' but there is no link or button. The monthly digest references 'sincronizate și scanate în aplicație' with no link either. FRONTEND_APP_URL exists in backend/src/config/env.js:42 ('http://localhost:5173') but is never imported by any template.
findings.problem: The single most important job of a security alert email is to drive the user back into the product to triage the threat. With zero links, the user must manually go find the app — friction at the exact moment urgency matters. An Apple-grade transactional email always has one obvious primary action.
findings.recommendation: Import FRONTEND_APP_URL into the template module and render a bulletproof (table-based, VML-fallback) pill button. Alert: deep-link to the inbox quarantine filter, e.g. `${FRONTEND_APP_URL}/inbox?riskBucket=quarantine`, label 'Review flagged emails'. Digest: `${FRONTEND_APP_URL}/dashboard`, label 'Open dashboard'. Style the primary button as bg #3b9eff, color #04111f (the app's --color-primary-foreground), 14px/600 weight, padding 14px 28px, border-radius 10px. Render it as a single-cell <table> with mso conditional <v:roundrect> so it survives Outlook.

findings.title: Three templates, three unrelated visual identities — none on-brand
findings.current: Welcome header is linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea,#764ba2) (purple). Digest header is flat #0f172a (slate). Alert header is linear-gradient(135deg,#dc2626,#991b1b) (red). Bodies sit on #f4f4f5 / #f3f4f6 light grey. The real brand is bg #0a0d14, card #11151f, primary #3b9eff, foreground #e7ecf3 (frontend/src/index.css:20-29).
findings.problem: A user who knows the dark cyan/blue SecureInbox app receives a purple-gradient welcome that looks like a generic Bootstrap starter, then a red email that looks like a different vendor. There is no shared header, no logo, no consistent accent. This destroys the 'trustworthy, one coherent product' feeling — fatal for a security brand where trust IS the product.
findings.recommendation: Build one shared shell helper (header band, card, footer) reused by all three templates. Header: deep brand surface #0a0d14 with a 1px hairline #1f2838 and the SecureInbox shield wordmark; accent rule in #3b9eff. Body card: white #ffffff is fine for light-mode legibility, but use the brand neutral ramp for text (#0f172a heads, #475569 body) and #3b9eff for links/CTAs across ALL three. Kill the purple and the loud red gradients in the chrome; reserve risk color for the risk content only.

findings.title: Risk colors are hardcoded and wrong vs the canonical 6-bucket palette
findings.current: Alert uses #dc2626/#991b1b/#fca5a5/#7f1d1d/#fef2f2/#fee2e2 for 'likely phishing'. The canonical quarantine (likely_phishing) color in frontend/src/index.css:49 is #f43f5e and confirmed_phishing is #b91c1c. The digest renders 'suspecte', 'probabil phishing', 'carantină', 'sigure' as identical plain rows (renderMetric, line 104) with no color at all — safe/suspicious/quarantine all look the same.
findings.problem: The whole app's premise is the 6-color risk language defined once in risk.js (the instructions say NEVER hardcode it). The email invents its own reds, so the alert color doesn't match the badge the user sees in-app. And the digest, the one place stats matter, applies zero risk color — the user can't visually scan safe-vs-danger.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the canonical hexes as inline constants in the template module with a comment pointing to risk.js: safe #34c77b, needs_review #f0b429, quarantine #f43f5e, confirmed_phishing #b91c1c, unscanned #8a96aa. In the alert use quarantine #f43f5e as the accent (not #dc2626). In renderMetric, give the safe/suspicious/likelyPhishing/quarantined rows a 4px left color bar (border-left:4px solid <hex>) and color the number to match, so the digest reads as a risk scoreboard at a glance.

findings.title: Outer layout is a <div>, not a table — fragile in Outlook and older clients
findings.current: Every template centers content with `<div style="max-width:600px;margin:0 auto">`. There is no role=presentation table wrapper, no MSO conditional, no <center>, no explicit width attributes. Stats are tables, but the page scaffold is not.
findings.problem: Outlook (Word rendering engine) ignores max-width on divs and does not reliably honor margin:0 auto — the email can render full-bleed left-aligned at desktop width. This is the classic reason 'beautiful' emails break. Not Apple-grade because it isn't bulletproof.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each template in the standard bulletproof scaffold: outer 100% table with bgcolor, an inner 600px fixed-width table (width=600 attribute + style), centered with align=center, plus an `<!--[if mso]><table width=600>...<![endif]-->` conditional. Add `<meta name=viewport content=width=device-width>`. Keep the inner content tables as-is.

findings.title: No dark-mode handling — risk of unreadable inverted text
findings.current: <head> contains only `<meta charset=UTF-8>`. No `<meta name=color-scheme>`, no `<meta name=supported-color-schemes>`, no dark-mode media query, no explicit bgcolor on text containers beyond the white card.
findings.problem: For a dark-only app, an email that ignores dark mode is jarring. Apple Mail/Gmail dark mode may auto-invert the white card and recolor text unpredictably — light grey #6b7280/#9ca3af footers can collapse to near-invisible, and the white logo/header text can vanish. Premium emails declare their color intent.
findings.recommendation: Add to <head>: `<meta name=color-scheme content="light dark">` and `<meta name=supported-color-schemes content="light dark">`. Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block setting the card to #11151f, text to #e7ecf3, hairlines to #1f2838, so the email becomes a true on-brand dark surface in dark clients while staying clean white in light clients. Set explicit bgcolor attributes on all table cells so auto-invert has less to guess.

findings.title: No preheader text — the inbox preview is wasted or leaks raw HTML
findings.current: Body opens straight into the layout div / gradient header. No hidden preheader span. The first visible text the inbox preview grabs for the alert is effectively the emoji/header.
findings.problem: The preheader is the second subject line — for a phishing alert it's prime real estate to convey 'N high-risk emails flagged, review now.' Leaving it empty means Gmail/Apple Mail show truncated header markup or '🚨 Phishing Alert SecureInbox detected...' awkwardly. Apple-grade emails always control the preview.
findings.recommendation:
Add a hidden preheader immediately after : `
${emailCount} high-risk email(s) flagged — review in SecureInbox.
` followed by the usual whitespace-hack span. Digest: '${monthLabel}: ${counts.scannedEmails} scanned, ${safeRate}% safe.'

findings.title: Emoji-as-icon (🚨 🎉 🎊 👤 📅 💬) instead of a real wordmark/logo
findings.current: Subjects and headers lean on emoji: welcome subject 'Bine ai venit, ${userName}! 🎉', a 48px 🚨 as the alert hero, 👤/📅 row labels in the welcome table.
findings.problem: Emoji render inconsistently across clients (Outlook desktop shows tofu/monochrome), look consumer-casual, and undermine the calm authority a security tool needs. A 48px siren emoji is exactly the 'drown the UI in alarm' anti-pattern the design goal warns against. There is no SecureInbox logo anywhere, so brand recall is zero.
findings.recommendation: Replace the siren with a restrained shield mark (inline SVG won't render in Gmail — use a hosted PNG @2x, ~40px, with alt='SecureInbox'). Drop emoji from subjects: 'Welcome to SecureInbox' / 'Sumar lunar de securitate — ${monthLabel}'. If you want a status glyph, use a small solid-color dot (8px round table cell) in the canonical risk hex, not an emoji.

findings.title: Typography is flat — no real scale, weak hierarchy, system fallback font
findings.current: Font stack is 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif (the app uses Inter). Body copy is 15px/1.6 #374151, metric labels 14-ish #4b5563, h1 26px, h2 18px. Line-height and letter-spacing are mostly default; numbers in metrics are just font-weight 700 at body size.
findings.problem: The hierarchy is shallow: the big stats (the reason to open a digest) are the same size as their labels. No tabular-figures alignment, no display-size hero number. 'Segoe UI' on macOS/iOS falls back to a different metric than the in-app Inter, so the email feels foreign. Not the legible, confident typographic scale Apple HIG calls for.
findings.recommendation: Set font stack to `-apple-system, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif` (Inter won't web-font reliably in email; SF-first is closest to the brand on Apple clients). Establish a scale: hero number 40px/700, section title 13px/600 uppercase letter-spacing 0.06em #64748b, body 15px/1.65 #334155, metric value 17px/700 with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Right-align numbers and give metric rows 14px vertical padding for breathing room.

findings.title: Digest stats are an undifferentiated 8-row table — no hero, no scannability
findings.current: Eight renderMetric rows in a row (synced, scanned, safe, suspicious, likely phishing, quarantined, reviewed, safe rate) all identical: label left grey, number right bold, 1px #e5e7eb divider. The safeRate % (the headline KPI) is the last, least-prominent row.
findings.problem: A monthly security report's job is to land one reassuring/alarming number instantly. Burying 'safe rate' as row 8 of an identical list means the user reads nothing. There's no visual grouping (volume vs risk vs review), no hero stat, no proportion/donut. This is a spreadsheet, not a premium summary.
findings.recommendation: Lead with a hero block: big 40px safeRate% in risk-safe #34c77b (or #f0b429 if <80%), subtitle 'of scanned emails were safe this month'. Then a 2x2 stat-card grid (table cells with bg #f8fafc, radius 12px, 16px padding) for the four risk buckets, each with its canonical color dot + label + count. Keep synced/scanned/reviewed as a smaller secondary table below. Optionally a horizontal stacked bar built from colored table cells whose widths are the bucket percentages.

findings.title: Mixed languages across templates (RO welcome+digest, EN alert)
findings.current: Welcome and monthly digest are in Romanian ('Bine ai venit', 'Sumar phishing', 'Emailuri sincronizate'). The phishing alert is entirely in English ('Phishing Alert', 'Please open SecureInbox', 'Hi ${userName}'). Footer of welcome is RO ('Toate drepturile rezervate'), alert footer is EN.
findings.problem: The same user gets RO and EN emails from one product. Inconsistent locale is an obvious polish failure and reads as 'cobbled together.' Premium products are locale-coherent.
findings.recommendation: Pick one locale per user and thread it through all templates (the app is RO-leaning per formatNumber/formatDate using ro-RO). Translate the alert to RO to match, or add a tiny locale param to all three template functions and a shared strings map. At minimum, make all three consistent in one pass.

findings.title: Generic, unbranded footer — no address, no real unsubscribe mechanics
findings.current: Welcome footer: '© 2026 Toate drepturile rezervate' only. Alert footer: a sentence telling users to go to 'Settings → Notifications' to disable — but no link. Digest has no footer at all beyond the period line.
findings.problem: No company name/address, no logo, no one-click manage-preferences link, hardcoded year '2026'. 'Go to Settings → Notifications' as plain text is a dead end. This both looks unfinished and risks spam-filtering for bulk security alerts. Apple-grade emails close with a quiet, complete, branded footer.
findings.recommendation: Build a shared footer: SecureInbox wordmark (muted), one line of muted #94a3b8 11px text, a real 'Manage notifications' link to `${FRONTEND_APP_URL}/settings/notifications`, and `© ${new Date().getFullYear()} SecureInbox`. Keep it on a subtle band (transparent on white, #0a0d14 in dark mode) separated by a 1px hairline, generous 32px top padding.

findings.title: Inconsistent radii, shadows, and spacing between templates
findings.current: Welcome/alert cards use border-radius 16px and box-shadow 0 4px 6px rgba; digest uses 8px radius and no shadow. Inner blocks vary: 12px (welcome), 8px and 10px (digest/alert). Header padding ranges 28-40px with no system.
findings.problem: Shadows often don't render in email anyway (Outlook drops them), and the radii are all over the place, so the family looks accidental. Depth in HIG should be subtle and consistent, not a 16px-vs-8px lottery.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one radius scale: outer card 14px, inner blocks 12px, pills/buttons 10px. Drop box-shadow (unreliable) in favor of a 1px #e2e8f0 hairline border for definition in light mode and #1f2838 in dark. Standardize header padding to 32px and body padding to 32px across all three via the shared shell.

findings.title: Welcome avatar circle relies on line-height centering that breaks in Outlook
findings.current: The initial-letter avatar is an 80x80 div with border-radius 50%, line-height:80px to vertically center the letter, inside a gradient header.
findings.problem: border-radius 50% renders as a square in Outlook desktop, and line-height vertical-centering inside a fixed-height div is unreliable across clients. A premium first-touch email shouldn't show a grey square with an off-center letter.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a hosted circular brand mark PNG, or render the avatar as a single-cell table with align=center valign=middle, width/height 72, bgcolor, and a Ghost-style mso conditional. Better: lead the welcome with the SecureInbox shield logo, not a user initial — it's a brand moment, not a profile chip.

findings.title: Alert email list lacks per-email risk context and sender domain emphasis
findings.current: Each flagged email row shows subject (bold) + 'From: ${email.from}' in small red. No domain highlight, no per-email verdict/score, no received time, no truncation guard beyond word-break.
findings.problem: In a phishing alert the sender domain is the most diagnostic field — that's how a user spots spoofing. It's buried in a run-on 'From:' string. There's also no per-row risk indicator even though scans carry a score/verdict.
findings.recommendation: Restructure each row as: subject 14px/600 #0f172a (truncate ~60 chars server-side), then a second line 'displayName <highlighted senderDomain>' where the domain is bold #f43f5e, plus a small relative time. Add a left 4px quarantine bar (#f43f5e) per row. If the alert payload can include score/verdict, show a tiny risk pill per email.

findings.title: Hardcoded copyright year and Bucharest-only date formatting
findings.current: Welcome footer hardcodes '© 2026'. formatDate forces timeZone 'Europe/Bucharest'; the alert uses a separate en-GB UTC string (send-email.js:226), so digest timestamps are Bucharest local while alert timestamps are UTC.
findings.problem: Hardcoded year rots; two different time zones across two emails is the kind of inconsistency a careful reviewer notices immediately. Minor but it reads as unpolished.
findings.recommendation: Use `new Date().getFullYear()` for the year. Pick one timezone strategy (the app's Europe/Bucharest) and apply it to the alert's detectedAt too, or label both with the zone ('14:32 EET'). Centralize date formatting in one helper used by all templates and send-email.js.

premiumOpportunities: Signature 'risk scoreboard' digest hero: one giant tabular-figure safe-rate % that changes color through the canonical ramp (#34c77b → #f0b429 → #f43f5e) based on the month's risk, with a subtitle that reads like a sentence ('No threats slipped through this month.' vs 'We blocked 7 likely-phishing attempts.'). Make the number the emotional payload of the whole email.

A pure-HTML stacked risk bar built from colored <td> cells whose widths are the bucket percentages (safe/suspicious/quarantine), with the canonical hexes and a tiny legend — gives an at-a-glance distribution with zero images, bulletproof everywhere including Outlook.

True dark-mode email that mirrors the app: in prefers-color-scheme:dark the card becomes #11151f on #0a0d14 with #e7ecf3 text and #3b9eff accents, so opening the email in Apple Mail dark mode feels like opening SecureInbox itself — a rare, premium touch most products skip.

One reusable email design system (shared header band + card + footer + button + risk-dot helpers) so welcome, digest, and alert become one coherent family; this is the single highest-leverage move for perceived quality.

Calm-confidence alert tone: replace the 48px siren and red gradient with a composed dark header, a single quarantine-colored accent, and a clear primary 'Review flagged emails' button — the email projects 'we caught it, you're in control' instead of panic, which is what a trustworthy security brand should feel like.

Deep-linked CTAs that drop the user exactly where they need to be (alert → /inbox?riskBucket=quarantine, digest → /dashboard, with the flagged email id when count is 1 → /emails/:id) using the already-available FRONTEND_APP_URL, turning the email into a true triage launchpad.

Per-email spoof spotlight in the alert: visually emphasize the sender domain (bold, risk-colored) and, if available, a one-line 'why it was flagged' pulled from the top triggered rule — educational and reassuring, reinforcing the product's explainable-AI thesis angle.

designDirection.summary: SecureInbox should feel like a calm, trustworthy security companion built by Apple: content-first, quietly confident, and tactile. The current UI is a competent dark shadcn dashboard that 'stops at sensible defaults' — small flat type, invisible shadows, ad-hoc tween motion, three clashing reds, and a verdict that whispers. The unified direction fixes the foundation once (a real type ramp, a dark-tuned elevation+material language, a single spring motion vocabulary, and a deliberate OKLCH-derived risk ramp) so every component inherits the upgrade for free. The product's emotional center is the risk verdict: safe states recede into calm green/neutral, and strong color (rose→brick red) is reserved strictly for real threats, so the eye is trained to trust color rather than ignore it. Stay dark-only for the thesis, but make the token layer theme-aware so light mode is a future flip, not a rewrite. The result: an inbox that scans effortlessly, a dashboard that answers 'am I safe?' in under a second, a reading view that protects you the moment you open a risky email, and a verdict moment that lands with one tasteful spring — never alarm-red walls, never gratuitous motion.
designDirection.colorAndType: COLOR — Keep the deep-navy base (bg #0a0d14, card #11151f, primary #3b9eff) which is already good. (1) Lighten muted-foreground from #8a96aa to ~#9aa6ba (≈5.5:1 on card) and add --color-muted-foreground-subtle ~#6b7689 for tertiary/disabled. (2) Rebuild the risk reds as ONE deliberate OKLCH severity ramp (same/related hue, rising chroma + falling lightness = more severe): quarantine ≈ oklch(0.62 0.20 18) ~#f0506b, confirmed_phishing ≈ oklch(0.50 0.20 22) ~#c43030, and set --color-destructive to a calmer desaturated member of the same family so action-red never competes with risk-red. (3) Lift the 'soft' risk backgrounds (currently near-black, quarantine-soft #2a1020 ≈ phishing-soft #220d0d) — derive them with color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-risk-X) ~14%, var(--color-background)) so badges/banners read as confident tinted pills and stay in lockstep with the base hue. (4) Add primary tonal tokens --color-primary-hover #57adff, --color-primary-active #2a8be6, --color-primary-soft; switch button hover from /90 opacity to the explicit hover token. TYPE — Self-host InterVariable.woff2 (preload, font-display:swap, weight 100–900), drop the render-blocking Google Fonts link, enable font-feature-settings 'cv11','ss01' + tabular-nums for numerals. Define a semantic ramp in @theme and drive all headings off it (rem @16px): --text-display 2.5rem/1.05/-0.02em, --text-h1 1.875rem/1.1/-0.018em, --text-h2 1.375rem/1.2/-0.012em, --text-h3 1.0625rem/1.3, --text-body 0.9375rem/1.5 (bump default body 14→15px), --text-sm 0.8125rem, --text-caption 0.75rem/+0.01em. Add a label-overline utility. FONT RECOMMENDATION: stay with Inter (self-hosted variable) — already the identity, free/thesis-safe, and InterVariable + cv11/ss01 closes most of the gap to SF; optionally Inter Display for >24px headings.
designDirection.motionPrinciples: One shared spring-physics vocabulary, exported from a new frontend/src/lib/motion.js and mirrored as CSS tokens in @theme, so JS (Framer) and CSS animations share one feel and can never drift. Springs (not duration tweens) carry all entrances, layout, and presses; tweens reserved only for pure color/opacity crossfades. Core constants: springSoft { type:'spring', stiffness:380, damping:32, mass:0.9 } for UI entrances/layout; springSnappy { stiffness:520, damping:30 } for press/toggles; ease [0.32,0.72,0,1] (Apple decelerate) for CSS; durations fast 180ms / base 260ms / slow 400ms. Standardize: every interactive element confirms touch with a subtle press (buttons whileTap scale 0.97, large rows/cards 0.99); entrance distance always y:8; hover adds 1px lift + shadow, never large jumps. Wrap the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion='user'> + a prefers-reduced-motion CSS guard so all motion degrades to instant/opacity-only — premium AND accessible. Motion is meaningful only: animate state changes (verdict resolves, row reviewed, scan completes), never re-display the same data (kill count-up-from-0-on-every-sync).
signatureMoves: Verdict reveal: when a scan completes or a manual review lands, the VerdictBanner cross-fades keyed on riskBucket with springSoft, its icon springs into a tinted ring, and (for quarantine/confirmed_phishing only) a single one-shot color-matched glow 'breath' fades over ~600ms and never repeats. Safe never animates loudly — calm authority, no alarm-red flashing.

Traveling selection: one shared Framer layoutId highlight that glides between sidebar items on desktop and bottom-nav tabs on mobile, with a thin primary accent bar that springs vertically — a single recognizable 'where am I' motion across both breakpoints; the same pattern powers the inbox filter segmented-control pill.

Privacy gate tied to risk: remote images blocked by default for needs_review/quarantine/confirmed_phishing emails with one calm inline 'Load images' affordance; auto-loaded for safe — the product visibly protects you the instant you open a risky message.

Posture hero on the dashboard: replace the four equal KPIs with a full-width 'You're protected' / 'N messages need your attention' band plus an interactive risk donut whose center reads the safe % (not a raw 'scanned' tally) and whose slices link to /inbox?riskBucket=X — answers 'am I safe?' in under a second.

iOS-grade switch + tactile mark-phishing: enlarge the settings switch to 28x46px with a spring thumb that elongates on press; replace the literal '✓' string on review buttons with an animated lucide Check that springs in, fire a Sonner toast ('Marked as phishing · Moved to Gmail Spam') and optimistically flip state instead of a full reload.

Dark-mode, on-brand transactional emails: one shared email shell (header band + card + footer + bulletproof CTA + risk-dot helpers) reused by welcome/digest/alert, using canonical risk hexes, deep-linked CTAs (alert → /inbox?riskBucket=quarantine), and a prefers-color-scheme:dark variant mirroring the app (#11151f on #0a0d14) so opening the email feels like opening SecureInbox.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Token foundation (color, type, elevation, motion, spacing)
phases.goal: Establish the single source of truth all components inherit from, with no component rewrites yet, so later phases compose cleanly and nothing else can drift.
changes: Self-host InterVariable.woff2: add @font-face (font-display:swap, weight 100 900), preload in index.html, remove the render-blocking Google Fonts <link>; add font-feature-settings 'cv11','ss01' + tabular-nums for numerals.
Add a semantic type ramp in @theme (--text-display/h1/h2/h3/body/sm/caption) each with paired line-height + letter-spacing; bump default body 14→15px; add a label-overline @utility.
Add a dark-tuned elevation ramp (--shadow-xs/sm/md/lg) + a top inner-highlight convention (inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.04)); start using the already-defined --color-elevated for real elevation.
Add motion tokens to @theme (--ease-out, --duration-fast/base/slow) and create frontend/src/lib/motion.js exporting springSoft, springSnappy, ease, dur.

Rebuild risk reds as one OKLCH severity ramp (quarantine/confirmed_phishing/destructive); lift the risk 'soft' tokens via color-mix — keep the exact token NAMES so risk.js and all utilities keep working.
Lighten --color-muted-foreground to ~#9aa6ba; add --color-muted-foreground-subtle; add --color-primary-hover/active/soft.
Add spacing/rhythm tokens (--space-section/block/stack, --gutter); bump container-page padding to clamp(1rem,4vw,2rem); rework radius ramp to derive from a base --radius and add --radius-2xl.

Wrap app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion='user'> in main.jsx + add a global prefers-reduced-motion guard in index.css; replace the universal '* { border-color }' reset with Tailwind v4 themed default border color (verify risk border-l-* still win).

phases.name: Phase 2 — Shared primitives (Button, Card, Input, Switch, Skeleton, new UI components)
phases.goal: Upgrade low-level shadcn primitives once so press/hover/spring/elevation/focus appear everywhere automatically, and add the missing components the pages need.
changes: Button: add active:scale-[0.97] + tactile timing to base cva, switch default hover to --color-primary-hover (not /90), add icon-sm (h-9 w-9) size and a primary hover glow; add optional MotionButton wrapper for whileTap/whileHover springs.
Card: add elevation tiers (flat KPI vs lifted hero) using new shadow tokens + inner highlight; add clickable-card hover lift (1px translate + shadow-md + border brighten).
Input: softer focus (ring-1 ring-primary/40 + soft halo) with transition-all ease, caret-primary; add a Textarea mirroring Input exactly; add a glass material utility for shell/login.
Switch: enlarge to ~28x46px, Framer spring thumb (springSnappy) with press elongation, smooth color sweep, distinct is-saving state.
Skeleton: replace animate-pulse with a left-to-right shimmer keyframe.
Add AlertDialog (Radix) + a base Dialog primitive — required by Settings disconnect; none exist today.
Adopt the orphaned PageHeader as the single page-title primitive (text-h1/h2 scale, muted description, actions slot).

phases.name: Phase 3 — App shell, navigation & page transitions
phases.goal: Make the chrome recede (material/depth) and give navigation one premium motion language across desktop and mobile.
changes: Sidebar: shared layoutId traveling active indicator (spring) + primary accent bar; whileTap press; frosted material (backdrop-blur-xl, softened divider, top-edge inner highlight); single-name wordmark + richer logo chip; cleaner footer rhythm; chevron + press on user dropdown.
BottomNav: layoutId active pill + whileTap on icon chip; safe-area-inset-bottom padding; replace magic-number FAB offset with calc(...+env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).

PageTransition: switch to springSoft, y:10, gate with useReducedMotion; add scroll-reset on pathname change; differentiate drill-down (Inbox→EmailDetail slides forward, Back slides back) vs top-level crossfade; fix the mode='wait' empty-beat (min-height or overlapping crossfade).
MobileSync FAB: AnimatePresence scale/opacity enter-exit + whileTap.
Adopt PageHeader on Dashboard/Inbox/Reports/Settings/EmailDetail so titles share one scale.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Inbox list, EmailRow, grouping & skeletons
phases.goal: Turn the inbox from a generic admin table into a calm, scannable, tactile triage queue.
changes: EmailRow: motion(Link) with capped-stagger entrance + whileTap; 3-step type hierarchy (sender 15px semibold / subject dimmer / snippet caption); deterministic monogram avatar anchor; focus-visible ring (currently none); remove duplicate border-b (let divide-y own separators); soften hover to neutral foreground/[0.03] + trailing ChevronRight reveal.

Risk emphasis via a single risk.js helper (tone.emphasis quiet|loud): safe/reviewed_safe/unscanned recede (no/faint bar, dot or icon-only badge), strong color reserved for needs_review/quarantine/confirmed_phishing.

Filter chips: add unscanned bucket, color each active chip by its risk tone, layoutId sliding indicator, count-as-pill; hide counts when a search q is active (monthly-summary counts can disagree with the list).
Fix sticky group headers (remove Card overflow-hidden, correct scroll model) or float headers with a hairline; InboxSkeleton mirrors real rows + group bands with varied widths + shimmer.
Search input: clear button, inline spinner while debouncing/loading, '/' focus shortcut, dim-in-place on refine instead of full skeleton swap.
Enlarge pagination touch targets (or move toward Load-more/infinite scroll) and bind the toolbar to the list card.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Security verdict UI (VerdictBanner, ScanDetails, RiskBadge, ReviewActions)
phases.goal: Make the verdict the hero with calm authority and deliver the signature verdict-reveal + tactile review feedback — the product's core moment.
changes: VerdictBanner: 2-line hero (40px tinted icon ring, text-h3/lg label, muted description, left accent), spring entrance, tiered emphasis by bucket (safe recedes; quarantine/phishing get ring + soft layered shadow + one-shot pulse), AnimatePresence keyed on riskBucket so verdict changes cross-fade, transition-colors on the tint; source label becomes a small pill with icon.

ReviewActions: animated lucide Check (spring) instead of '✓' string; Sonner success toasts incl. the Gmail-Spam side effect; optimistic state flip instead of full load(); show the consequence as helper text BEFORE the action; align phishing CTA color with quarantine rose (record in DECISIONS.md).

ScanDetails: restructure into a narrative — AI explanation as the primary panel (larger, breathing room, tinted chip), score bars + triggered rules demoted into a collapsed-by-default 'Evidence' group that staggers in; animate score-bar fills from 0 with springSoft (replace transition-all); color Total-score bar with the verdict tone; severity accent + sort on rule rows; reframe the Ollama-fallback as a calm info note using risk-review tokens (not hardcoded amber-*).

Privacy gate: in sanitizeEmailHtml, for needs_review/quarantine/confirmed_phishing rewrite img src→data-src and render a calm inline 'Load images' banner in EmailBody; auto-load for safe.
Keyboard nav: ←/→ or j/k for prev/next, Esc back, guarded against inputs; add a 'n of total' indicator; bump prev/next to icon-sm; keep a 'Back to inbox' when deep-linked without list context.
Detail entrance: own spring (opacity/y/scale) with small stagger (verdict→header→body); directional slide between prev/next via AnimatePresence; dim stale body while loading.

Reading surface: drop the double-bordered inset box, sit body on the card with a max reading width (~68ch); stronger subject/sender hierarchy + monogram; plain-text fallback uses full foreground + capped width; collapse ScanDetails by default; relative-but-precise date matching the inbox.
Re-scan: elevate to a clear secondary action with feedback (toast + animated badge change).

phases.name: Phase 7 — Dashboard + RiskDonut + StatCard
phases.goal: Reframe the first screen as a calm security posture answer, not a metrics grid.
changes: Add a full-width posture hero band: 'You're protected' (risk-safe) vs 'N messages need your attention' (risk-quarantine) with a CTA to /inbox?riskBucket=quarantine; demote Scanned/Synced to a caption; PageHeader greeting with account email + last-synced.

RiskDonut: enlarge (~210px), pull colors/labels from getRiskMeta (no hand-mapped vars), center shows safe % (not raw 'scanned'), legend↔slice hover linking with activeShape, custom card-matching tooltip, include unscanned or relabel center honestly, percentages in legend.

StatCard: link threat cards to inbox filters with whileHover lift + whileTap + ArrowRight reveal; raise value to text-3xl tabular-nums; quiet the icon tile; sentence-case label; count-up only on real value change + reduced-motion guard (refactor to shared parent-variant stagger, drop manual staggerIndex).

Attention list: slimmer dashboard row variant that drops the redundant per-row badge and surfaces the strongest scan signal; success-empty 'All clear' in risk-safe-soft with a one-time spring shield; skeletons that mirror real layouts with crossfade; richer disconnected first-run hero; responsive gaps/type.

AI-analysis card: stop coloring infra 'Failed' with risk-review amber — use neutral/operational treatment; add count-up parity with StatCards.

Establish stat hierarchy (hero threats-found + plain-language headline, demote synced/scanned, tint bucket cards' left border); send-report success state on the button + 'last emailed' line; remove the double error surface (toast + ErrorState); add ReportsSkeleton; card descriptions; calm all-clear month state.

phases.name: Phase 9 — Settings + Login front door
phases.goal: Bring the two bookend surfaces to Apple-grade: a grouped, deferential settings screen with a safe destructive flow, and a confident, animated sign-in.
changes: Settings: gate Disconnect Gmail behind the new AlertDialog (blocker — currently one unguarded click wipes all app data); page header; single max-w-2xl grouped-list layout; card titles back to text-base + descriptions + tinted icon chips; clickable toggle rows with hover/press; richer connected-account row with live status; dirty-state + success micro-confirmation on saves; use the new Textarea in Support; staggered entry.

phases.name: Phase 10 — Cross-cutting motion sweep & cleanup
phases.goal: Replace every remaining ad-hoc tween with the shared vocabulary and verify nothing regressed.
changes: Audit all Framer/CSS animations to import from lib/motion.js; replace the five inline tween objects; standardize entrance distance and durations; ensure all collapse/disclosure carets are driven by the same spring as their panels.
Verify reduced-motion across every surface; confirm tabular-nums on all data numerals; remove dead code (orphan fragments, manual staggerIndex prop, inline pulse bars).
Run lint + frontend tests + build; manual end-to-end pass per docs/MANUAL_TESTS.md; update docs (DECISIONS, PROGRESS, TODO, ARCHITECTURE).

changes: Build one shared email shell (table-based bulletproof scaffold + MSO conditional, header band, card, footer, risk-dot + bulletproof CTA helpers) reused by all three templates.
Add CTA buttons (blocker — alert tells users to act but has no link): import FRONTEND_APP_URL, alert→/inbox?riskBucket=quarantine, digest→/dashboard.

Mirror canonical risk hexes (comment pointing to risk.js); kill the purple/red gradients and the 48px siren emoji; add a hosted shield wordmark; preheader text; color-scheme meta + prefers-color-scheme:dark variant mirroring the app; one locale per user; complete branded footer with real manage-notifications link + dynamic year.

Digest hero (big safe-rate % colored by ramp + 2x2 risk-card grid + optional HTML stacked risk bar); alert per-email rows emphasize sender domain + risk bar; consistent radii/spacing; fix avatar/timezone inconsistencies; SF-first font stack + real type scale.

openQuestions: Dark-only vs light mode: keep dark-only for the thesis demo (lower risk, less work) but build the token layer theme-aware so light is a future flip? Or invest in a real light theme now? Recommendation: theme-aware tokens, ship dark-only.

Font: stay with Inter self-hosted as InterVariable (free, already the identity, closes most of the gap to SF), or evaluate a paid/SF-like display face for headings? Recommendation: self-hosted InterVariable, optional Inter Display for large headings.
Product naming: the app is 'SecureInbox' in docs but 'XAI Phishing Shield' in login copy, index.html <title>, and email subjects. Which is the single canonical name to standardize everywhere?

How bold on motion/atmosphere: are signature flourishes (login 'shield activates' draw-on, living ambient background, dashboard posture ring/gauge replacing the donut, swipe-to-act on mobile, ⌘K command palette) in scope, or keep strictly to calm/minimal polish for the thesis timeline?

Dashboard data restructure: OK to replace the four equal KPI cards with a posture hero + interactive donut, and change the donut center from raw 'scanned' to 'safe %' (and include/relabel the unscanned bucket so the chart is honest)? This changes what the first screen emphasizes.

Inbox triage scope: numbered pagination vs infinite scroll / Load-more; and do you want the bigger triage features (swipe-to-act, reviewed rows dimming/settling in place, pinned 'Needs attention' band) or just row/typography/motion polish? Note: 'unread/reviewed' dimming depends on whether the backend exposes a read/reviewed flag.

Filter-count correctness: chip counts come from a monthly-summary query while the list is the full paged dataset, so they can disagree. Acceptable to hide counts during search (quick fix), or should the emails endpoint return a counts block scoped to the active search (backend change)?

Email privacy gate: confirm we should block remote images by default for risky buckets (needs_review/quarantine/confirmed_phishing) with a 'Load images' control — this changes reading behavior and is a deliberate trust feature.
Email locale: should all three transactional templates be unified to Romanian (the app is ro-RO-leaning), to English, or become per-user locale-driven?

Phishing-CTA color decision: align the mark-phishing affordance with the brighter rose quarantine (matches the danger language users already read) and reserve the dark brick #b91c1c for the confirmed state — confirm so it can be recorded in DECISIONS.md.
quickWins: Self-host InterVariable + drop the Google Fonts blocking link and enable cv11/ss01/tabular-nums — instant, app-wide typographic polish (Phase 1).
Add active:scale-[0.97] and the explicit primary-hover token to the shadcn Button base — tactile press feedback everywhere from one line (Phase 2).
Wrap the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion='user'> + add the prefers-reduced-motion CSS guard — premium accessibility baseline in minutes (Phase 1).
Lighten muted-foreground to ~#9aa6ba and lift the risk 'soft' backgrounds via color-mix — fixes borderline contrast and makes risk badges read as confident pills (Phase 1).
Adopt the already-built-but-orphaned PageHeader on every page — consistent titles/hierarchy with code that already exists (Phases 2–3).
Add Sonner success toasts to ReviewActions and replace the literal '✓' string with an animated Check — turns the core action from amateur to satisfying (Phase 5).
Soften EmailRow hover to neutral + add a focus-visible ring (currently none) — fixes an a11y gap and the brand-blue wash fighting risk colors (Phase 4).
Add the missing .email-body CSS rules — the single most-viewed content currently renders with raw browser defaults (Phase 6).
Remove the Reports double error surface (toast + full ErrorState) and color infra 'Failed' neutrally instead of risk-amber (Phase 8).
Swap skeleton animate-pulse for a shimmer keyframe — small change, noticeably more premium loading (Phase 2).
risks: Risk-token recolor (Phase 1) touches the whole app via risk.js; if soft-token names change, badges/banners/charts could break. De-risk: keep token NAMES identical, only change values (or switch TONES.soft to color-mix), and visually diff every risk surface (inbox, badge, banner, donut, reports) before merging.

Replacing the universal '* { border-color }' reset can change borders globally and may let risk border-l-* utilities lose/win specificity unexpectedly. De-risk: verify Tailwind v4 themed default-border behavior and grep every border-l-risk-* usage after the change.

Self-hosting InterVariable can cause FOUT/missing-glyph or a wrong weight if @font-face or preload is misconfigured. De-risk: keep a system-font fallback in the stack, test the preload path, confirm the Vite asset path in build.

Spring physics + AnimatePresence mode changes (page transitions, verdict cross-fade, list stagger) can introduce layout jumps, double-mount flashes (StrictMode), or scroll glitches. De-risk: cap list stagger, set min-heights where content swaps, test back/forward and deep-links, verify reduced-motion fallbacks.

Optimistic review state + removing the full reload (Phase 5) could desync UI from server if the request fails. De-risk: roll back optimistic state on error + surface an error toast; keep a refetch on failure.

The image privacy gate (Phase 6) modifies the sanitizer; a bug could break safe-email rendering or leak images on risky ones. De-risk: unit-test sanitizeEmailHtml per bucket and confirm safe still auto-loads while risky uses data-src.

Sticky-header / overflow-hidden changes on the inbox Card can alter clipping of rounded corners, focus rings, and pagination. De-risk: test with >10 rows across breakpoints and verify focus-visible rings render fully.

Filter-count fix: if counts are hidden during search but expected by tests/users, behavior changes; the deeper backend counts-block option is a larger change. De-risk: start with hide-on-search, defer the backend change behind an open question.

Email template overhaul (Phase 11) risks client-rendering regressions (Outlook, Gmail dark mode). De-risk: bulletproof table scaffold + MSO conditionals; test in Gmail + Apple Mail light/dark (ideally Litmus/Email-on-Acid) before shipping.

Scope creep from signature flourishes (posture ring, ⌘K, swipe-to-act, ambient login) against the thesis timeline. De-risk: treat them as opt-in via the open-questions answers; the phased plan delivers a fully premium result even if every flourish is cut.
